source_refs.note: Topic 3.1.1, printed page 47 (Figure 3.1, carried by the Lewis bonds original).

blocks.text: According to the Lewis theory, the ionic bond is formed by the complete transfer of electrons from an atom with low ionization energy to another atom with high electron affinity. The sodium atom (Na, 2, 8, 1) tends to lose its outermost electron to form the Na+ ion (2, 8), which has the electron configuration of neon, the noble gas nearest to it. The chlorine atom (2, 8, 7) gains one electron to form the chloride ion Cl- (2, 8, 8), also gaining the next noble gas electron arrangement. The oppositely charged Na+ and Cl- ions are held together by a strong ionic bond in the crystal of NaCl. A similar type of bond is expected between the metals of groups 1 and 2 and the elements of groups 16 and 17.

blocks.prompt: Magnesium is 2, 8, 2 and oxygen is 2, 6. Describe the ionic bond in magnesium oxide by the Lewis theory.
blocks.explanation: Magnesium, a group 2 metal with low ionization energy, loses both outer electrons to become Mg2+ (2, 8, like neon). Oxygen, a group 16 element with high electron affinity, gains the two electrons to become O2- (2, 8, like neon). The oppositely charged ions attract strongly in the MgO crystal.

items: Ionic bond: complete transfer of electrons from an atom of low ionization energy to one of high electron affinity; Na (2, 8, 1) gives Na+ (2, 8) and Cl (2, 8, 7) gives Cl- (2, 8, 8), held by strong attraction. Expected between groups 1 and 2 and groups 16 and 17.
